flags.note: Right passage, wrong code. "Without ever running out of money" is not a forward-looking absolute promise; it describes the output of a bounded historical dataset (every 30-year period 1970-2025), which the firm could substantiate from its backtest workpapers, so C6 is weak on its own. The text still warrants reviewer attention under C5: this is model/backtested performance presented with no criteria, assumptions, risks or limitations - no asset allocation or rebalancing assumptions, no statement of whether returns are net of advisory fees, trading costs or taxes, no note that 1970-2025 yields overlapping rather than independent 30-year windows, and no acknowledgment that the model was constructed with knowledge of that same history. The generic footer "past performance does not guarantee future results" does not carry the specific 6.5% withdrawal figure. Secondary exposure: the 6.5% figure has no net-of-fee treatment (C2-adjacent) and the favorable outcome is stated without counterweight on sequence-of-returns risk or lower forward returns (C9-adjacent). Worth a reviewer's time; redirect the theory from C6 to C5.
